text: The Wurtz reaction joins two molecules. Two bromoethane molecules with sodium in dry ether: the sodium takes both bromines, and the two ethyl groups bond together, giving butane. It doubles the carbon chain, so from a single halide it can only make alkanes with an even number of carbons. Mixing two halides gives a messy mixture of three alkanes.
